backup.sentence.failedDefault: The last run failed and the node did not say why.
backup.sentence.neverRunScheduled: This has never produced a snapshot. Run it once by hand rather than finding out on the day you need it.
backup.sentence.neverRunManual: This has never run. It has no schedule, so nothing will happen until you press the button.
backup.sentence.disabled: Switched off. Its {count} existing snapshot is still there and still restorable.
backup.sentence.disabledPlural: Switched off. Its {count} existing snapshots are still there and still restorable.
backup.sentence.manualKept: {count} snapshot kept. No schedule, so it runs when you press the button.
backup.sentence.manualKeptPlural: {count} snapshots kept. No schedule, so it runs when you press the button.
backup.sentence.scheduledKept: {count} snapshot kept, newest first. Keeping {retention} of them, or {days} days, whichever is smaller.
backup.sentence.scheduledKeptPlural: {count} snapshots kept, newest first. Keeping {retention} of them, or {days} days, whichever is smaller.
backup.snapshotSentence.running: Still being written. It cannot be restored from until the node finishes and reports it.
backup.snapshotSentence.failed: This snapshot failed and the node did not say why.
backup.snapshotSentence.deleted: Off the list. The archive itself goes when the node next prunes.
backup.snapshotSentence.activeRestore: A restore from this snapshot is running right now.
backup.snapshotSentence.proven: Restored successfully at least once, so this one is known to work.
backup.snapshotSentence.unproven: Never restored. A backup nobody has restored is a backup nobody knows about - verifying takes one press and touches nothing live.
backup.destSentence.disabled: Switched off. Nothing new is written here; what is already stored stays.
backup.destSentence.unproven: Never checked. Press Check before you point a backup at it - a destination that cannot be written to fails silently at three in the morning.
backup.destSentence.localReachable: Reachable. It lives on the node, so it survives a lost container and not a lost machine.
backup.restoreSentence.queued: Queued. A node picks it up on its next pass.
backup.restoreSentence.runningInPlace: Restoring over the live data. A snapshot of what was there was taken first.
backup.restoreSentence.runningVerify: Restoring somewhere disposable to prove the archive is good. Nothing live is touched.
backup.restoreSentence.succeededInPlace: Done. The data is back as it was in the snapshot.
backup.restoreSentence.succeededVerify: Done. This snapshot restores, so it is a backup you can rely on.
backup.restoreSentence.failed: It failed, and the node did not say why.
backup.schedule.noSchedule: No schedule - runs only when you press the button
backup.schedule.monthly: On day {day} of every month at {time}{zone}
backup.tabs.label: Backup sections
backup.list.title: Backups
backup.list.description: The node does the copying and pushes straight to your destination; nothing passes through the panel. Restoring is one press, and verifying a snapshot without touching anything live is another.
backup.list.noDestTitle: There is nowhere to put a backup yet
backup.list.noDestDesc: A schedule needs a destination - an S3-compatible bucket, or a path on the node itself. Add one and check it before you rely on it.

backup.list.unproven.one: One schedule has never produced a snapshot. Run them once by hand rather than finding out on the day you need them.
backup.list.unproven.other: {count} schedules have never produced a snapshot. Run them once by hand rather than finding out on the day you need them.

backup.list.plan.title: Your plan
backup.list.plan.description: What this organization's plan allows for backups.
backup.list.noOrg.title: Nothing to back up yet
backup.list.noOrg.desc: Backups belong to an organization, and you are not a member of one. Create one, or ask somebody to invite you, and this page fills in.
backup.policy.label: backup schedules
backup.policy.empty.title: Nothing is being backed up
backup.policy.empty.description: A schedule copies one volume or one database to a destination, keeps the last few, and prunes the rest. Until there is one, nothing here is protected against a mistake or a lost disk.
backup.policy.deleteConfirm.title: Delete “{name}”?
backup.policy.deleteConfirm.body: Nothing is copied under this policy again. Every snapshot it has already taken stays where it is and stays restorable.
backup.snapshots.title: Snapshots
backup.snapshots.description: Each one is a point you can go back to. Restoring puts it over the live data after taking a snapshot of what is there now; verifying restores it somewhere disposable and throws the copy away.

backup.snapshots.unproven.one: One snapshot has never been restored. Verifying one takes a few minutes and touches nothing live - it is the difference between having backups and knowing they work.
backup.snapshots.unproven.other: {count} of your {total} restorable snapshots have never been restored. Verifying one takes a few minutes and touches nothing live - it is the difference between having backups and knowing they work.

backup.snapshots.storageUsedDesc: Across every destination this organization writes to.
backup.snapshotList.label: snapshots
backup.snapshotList.empty.title: No snapshots yet
backup.snapshotList.empty.desc: A schedule produces these, and so does pressing Run now on one. Until there is at least one, there is nothing to restore from.
backup.snapshotList.restoreConfirm.title: Restore {target} from this snapshot?
backup.snapshotList.restoreConfirm.body: Everything in {target} is replaced by what was there when this snapshot was taken. Anything written since is gone from the live copy - a snapshot of the current data is taken first, so it can be put back, but that is another restore and more minutes.
backup.snapshotList.deleteConfirm.title: Delete this snapshot?
backup.snapshotList.deleteConfirm.body: It comes off the list now and the archive itself goes when the node next prunes. If it is the only copy of something, there will be no way back to it.
backup.destinations.title: Destinations
backup.destinations.description: Where your snapshots are pushed. The node writes to them directly, so the panel being down does not stop a backup and the panel being compromised does not hand anybody your archives.
backup.destList.empty.title: No destinations yet
backup.destList.empty.desc: A backup needs somewhere to go. An S3-compatible bucket is the useful answer - it survives the machine - and a path on the node is there for the cases where offsite is not an option.
backup.destList.platformNotice: Provided by the platform. Anybody here can back up to it; only an operator can change it.
backup.destList.readOnlyNotice: Your role here is read-only, so this is shown but not editable.
backup.destList.cannotDelete: It cannot be deleted while a schedule points at it or a snapshot sits on it.
backup.destList.deleteConfirm.title: Delete “{name}”?
backup.destList.deleteConfirm.body: Nothing stored there is touched. The panel just stops offering it as somewhere to write.
backup.destForm.description: Snapshots are pushed here by the node itself. The panel never holds a copy, so this is the only place they exist.
backup.destForm.name: Name
backup.destForm.hintLocal: On the node. It survives a container being lost and not the machine being lost, so it is a convenience rather than a backup strategy.
backup.destForm.hintS3: Anything speaking the S3 API: AWS, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Garage, Hetzner.
backup.destForm.localPathHint: Has to be under {root}. The daemon can write nowhere else - its systemd unit restricts it.
backup.destForm.regionHint: Some providers do not care; the signature does.
backup.destForm.pathPrefixHint: Optional. Keeps these snapshots in one folder of a bucket you use for other things too.
backup.destForm.secretHintEdit: Leave empty to keep the one already stored. It is encrypted and never shown again.
backup.destForm.secretHintNew: Stored encrypted. Nothing in the panel displays it afterwards.
backup.destForm.storageClassHint: Optional. A cold class is cheaper to keep and slower - and sometimes dearer - to restore from.
backup.destForm.enabledHint: Off stops anything new being written here. What is already stored stays and is still restorable.
backup.adminDest.title: Backup destinations
backup.adminDest.description: Shared by every organization on this platform. A tenant sees them on their own destinations page and can point a schedule at one, but cannot change or delete it.

backup.adminDest.unchecked.one: One enabled destination has never been checked. Every tenant on the platform can point a schedule at these, so a bucket with the wrong credentials fails for all of them at once - and quietly.
backup.adminDest.unchecked.other: {count} enabled destinations have never been checked. Every tenant on the platform can point a schedule at these, so a bucket with the wrong credentials fails for all of them at once - and quietly.

backup.scheduleForm.descEdit: What it copies cannot be changed - the snapshots it has already taken belong to that. Everything else can.
backup.scheduleForm.descNew: Pick what to copy, where to put it, and how often. The node does the work and pushes straight to the destination; nothing passes through the panel.
backup.scheduleForm.name: Name
backup.scheduleForm.nameHint: You type this back to delete the policy, so make it one you would recognise.
backup.scheduleForm.whatToCopyHint: A volume is copied with a short pause on writes; a database is dumped logically.
backup.scheduleForm.noDestHint: There is no enabled destination to write to. Add one under Destinations first.
backup.scheduleForm.destHint: Check a destination before you rely on it - an unwritable bucket fails at three in the morning.
backup.scheduleForm.cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
backup.scheduleForm.timezoneHint: An IANA name, such as Europe/Berlin. The schedule above is read in it.
backup.scheduleForm.enabledHint: Off stops new snapshots. The ones already taken stay and are still restorable.
backup.scheduleForm.presetNone: No schedule - only when I press the button
backup.scheduleForm.presetMonthly: On the 1st of each month at 03:00
backup.scheduleForm.presetCustom: A cron expression of my own
backup.restoreRun.title: Restore of {target}
backup.restoreRun.heading: Restoring {target}
backup.restoreRun.followingNotice: This page follows it on its own.
backup.restoreRun.safetyDesc: Before anything was overwritten, a snapshot was taken of the data that was there. If this restore turns out to have been the wrong one, that snapshot is what you restore next.
backup.restoreRun.progressDesc: The node's own log, as it reports it.
backup.restoreRun.emptyFinished: The node finished without sending a log. Nothing is missing - a small restore has little to say.
backup.restoreRun.emptyRunning: Nothing yet. A restore emits a handful of lines over several minutes, and they appear here as the node sends them.
backup.history.title: Restores
backup.history.description: Including the verify runs, which restore somewhere disposable and throw the result away. Those are what turn “we take backups” into “we have restored this one”.
backup.history.empty.title: Nothing has been restored yet
backup.history.empty.desc: Pick a snapshot and press Verify. It restores alongside the live data, checks the archive is good and throws the copy away, so it costs nothing but a few minutes and it is the only way to know a backup works.
